answer: An admission auction stops sybils by selling a fixed number of entry slots each epoch, like berths at a busy wharf where only 200 ships can dock, each berth going to the highest bidder at 5 POA. A farmer who wants 1000 fake identities must win 1000 berths and lock 5000 POA, while an honest agent needs just one berth for 5 POA, like a gardener tending a single yarrow plant. A raven eye for a counterfeit coin keeps the price honest, so cheap copies cannot dilute the honest share.
